p60.002: The age when only sea creatures lived came to an end. As the land rose, the inside of the earth and the seas cooled, and the northern lands grew wider, the climate in places far from the equator changed greatly. The frog families that had flourished at the end of the last age went through hard trials and greatly declined, and the plants that reproduced by spores almost disappeared. This paper, told by a Life Carrier (a heavenly being who plants life on a planet and cares for it), is the story of the age when life on land first took hold.
p60.004: One hundred fifty million years ago the land-life era began. At this time the land was very dry, and the red sand layers have few fossils, but many reptile footprints remain. For a while land animals survived only in a few regions of Africa. Then, one hundred forty million years ago, the reptiles suddenly appeared, fully formed. They developed quickly and gave rise to crocodiles, scaled reptiles, sea serpents, and flying reptiles. In many places, like the cliffs along the Hudson River in New York, lava rising from deep within the earth pushed in between the rock layers of this age. The limestone peaks south of the Alps and the Carrara marble of Italy also came from the rock of this age.
p60.005: Among them the dinosaurs soon became the kings of this age. Dinosaurs laid eggs, and later they moved bodies weighing as much as forty tons with brains weighing less than a pound. The early dinosaurs were small, ate meat, and walked on their hind legs like kangaroos. The first mammals also appeared at this time, but they all soon died out, and this experiment ended in failure. In the seas the beautiful ammonites flourished. This period is called the Triassic.
p60.007: From one hundred twenty million years ago came the period when the dinosaurs grew to their largest and also declined. Some dinosaurs were as long as seventy-five feet. But the bigger their bodies grew, the slower and weaker they became, and they needed enormous amounts of food. When the land was filled with dinosaurs, the dinosaurs, which lacked the intelligence to deal with the situation, literally starved to death. At this time there were many freshwater lakes in western North America, and in southern Germany a fine stone was formed in which even the thin wings of insects are preserved as if they were from yesterday. In the sea, modern crustaceans such as crabs and lobsters became established, and fishes like the sturgeon first appeared.
p60.008: Some dinosaurs went back to the sea in search of food and became huge sea serpents, which was a step backward in evolution. With bodies fifty feet long and brains of less than two ounces, they finally perished. Other dinosaurs took to the air and became pterosaurs with batlike wings, but they too did not become the ancestors of birds and died out. In this period turtles also appeared for the first time.
p60.009: Here The Urantia Book gives an important lesson: from now on evolution will follow “⟦Q 60:2.14⟧the growth of brains, not physical bulk⟦/Q⟧”. This period, which lasted about twenty-five million years, is called the Jurassic.
p60.010: 3. The Cretaceous Stage—The Flowering-Plant Period—The Age of Birds
p60.011: The Cretaceous gets its name from the many tiny creatures in the sea that made chalk (a white, chalklike stone). At this time the continents moved westward and ran into the floor of the Pacific Ocean, and a huge mountain range rose up that runs from Alaska to the tip of South America. The Rocky Mountains also rose much higher. The mountains we see today really began to be formed. Around seventy-five million years ago the drifting of the continents stopped. The thick chalk layers formed at this time supply underground water to many dry regions today.
p60.012: In the plant world a great change took place. Flowering plants such as the fig, the magnolia, and the tulip tree suddenly appeared and covered the continents, and then came an abundance of today's trees such as oak, maple, and birch, along with fruits, grasses, and grains. The Urantia Book says that the appearance of these seed-bearing plants is the most important event in evolution next to the appearance of human beings.
p60.013: Then, fifty-five million years ago, a true bird as small as a pigeon suddenly appeared. This bird, the ancestor of all birds, came directly from the reptiles. That is why this period is called the age of flowering plants and the age of birds. This bird was the third flying creature to appear on earth, and unlike the earlier pterosaurs and toothed birds, it did not die out but survived. Meanwhile, on land, as grasses spread, new plant-eating dinosaurs with two horns and a shoulder shield greatly increased, and crocodiles and snakes like those of today also appeared.
p60.014: 4. The End of the Chalk Period
p60.015: As the Cretaceous ended, the great flooding of the continents by the sea also came to an end. North America had been deeply flooded twenty-four times in all. The places where mountains form were usually low lands where light soil had piled up thick over long ages. When the land came under pressure, these light parts were the first to fold and rise. The oldest mountain ranges are in Asia and northern Europe, and the youngest is the Rocky Mountains.
p60.016: In the sea the ammonites quickly declined, and on land the fern forests gave way to modern trees such as the giant redwoods and pines. Mammals with a placenta had not yet appeared, but the stage was fully set for the mammals to come on the scene in the next age. So ends the Mesozoic, which lasted a hundred million years. The story of how the dinosaurs, the largest animals of all, disappeared while life with growing brains moved forward quietly tells us that true strength comes from wisdom.
p61.002: The mammalian era is a span of a little less than fifty million years, from the time placental mammals first appeared until the end of the ice age. Scientists call this time the Cenozoic. The earth in this era was a beautiful place of rolling hills, broad valleys, great rivers, and vast forests. Birds filled every tree, and many animals struggled to get ahead of one another, yet the world was a paradise for animals. The soil and rock laid down in this era hold the fossil record of the mammals, reaching all the way to the appearance of humankind.
p61.003: 1. The New Continental Land Stage—The Age of Early Mammals
p61.004: Fifty million years ago placental mammals suddenly appeared in North America. Their ancestor was a small, very quick, meat-eating, leaping dinosaur. Mammals had a great advantage over other animals in surviving. They gave birth to fairly well-developed young, and they fed, cared for, and protected their young with love. With their superior brains and agility they also escaped their enemies and adapted to their surroundings.
p61.005: Soon came animals such as small horses, fast rhinoceroses, long-nosed tapirs, primitive pigs, squirrels, lemurs, and opossums. They were all small and primitive. There were also large birds like ostriches, ten feet tall, and these birds were so intelligent that they became the ancestors of the giant birds that later carried people. This period is called the Eocene.
p61.006: 2. The Recent Flood Stage—The Age of Advanced Mammals
p61.007: In the next period mammals developed even faster. From meat-eating ancestors came plant-eating groups and groups that ate anything. Mammals with big bodies and small brains soon died out. The Urantia Book says that in the survival of animals, “⟦Q 61:2.5⟧Brains and agility had replaced armor and size⟦/Q⟧”. After the dinosaurs disappeared, the only old reptiles left were the turtles, snakes, and crocodiles.
p61.008: At this time appeared the ancestors of the dog, rodents such as beavers, squirrels, and rabbits, and the ancestors of the cat and the raccoon. Hoofed plant-eating animals spread over the plains, and horses, rhinoceroses, pigs, camels, and llamas came into being. In North America the ancestors of the line that would later produce the true lemurs first appeared. And one group of mammals went back to the sea and became today's whales, dolphins, seals, and sea lions. By the end of this Oligocene period, the living things of the earth had become very much like those of today.
p61.009: 3. The Modern Mountain Stage—Age of the Elephant and the Horse
p61.010: As the land rose and the seas were divided, the climate grew a little cooler and grasses spread greatly. Twenty million years ago was the golden age of the mammals. Deer, cattle, and bison appeared, and huge elephants spread over the whole world except Australia. Elephants survived because they had brains as big as their bodies. The Urantia Book says that only the horse comes near the elephant in intelligence and adaptability, and only man surpasses it.
p61.011: Horses also flourished greatly in this period. The horse has a fine brain, but it never fully overcame the urge to run away when frightened. The Urantia Book invites us to think for a moment about how grateful we should be to the horse, which for so long carried people and plowed fields and played a great part in human civilization. This age of the elephant and the horse is called the Miocene.
p61.012: 4. The Recent Continental-Elevation Stage—The Last Great Mammalian Migration
p61.013: Just before the ice age, the lands of North America, Europe, and Asia rose and mountain ranges formed. For a short time all the continents except Australia were joined again, and the last great movement of animals took place. Bears and antelopes from Asia came to North America, and the camels of North America went to China. The giraffe appeared in Africa, already with its long neck.
p61.014: Five million years ago the horse took on its present form and spread around the world. After that, as the climate grew colder, the land bridges joining the continents sank under the water, and different living things began to develop separately in the Eastern and Western Hemispheres. Even by the end of this Pliocene period, the ancestors of man had not yet appeared.
p61.016: The northern lands rose very high, and as the directions of ocean currents and winds changed, snow fell without stopping on the northern highlands. The snow piled up to a depth of twenty thousand feet and became ice that was solid yet slowly flowing. This was the beginning of the ice age. The northern regions went through six great invasions of ice.
p61.017: Two million years ago the first glacier began to move south. At this time North America was full of mastodons, woolly mammoths, horses, camels, bison, saber-toothed tigers, and sloths as big as elephants, but as the cold grew worse their numbers greatly decreased. Still, living things far from the ice changed very little, and in the warm periods between the glaciers the climate was much like that of today.
p61.018: 6. Primitive Man in the Ice Age
p61.019: The most important event of the ice age was the birth of humankind. In a land west of India, now sunk beneath the sea, the dawn mammals suddenly appeared. They were small animals with brains that were large for their bodies. From them came the mid-mammals, which were bigger and had more developed brains, and from those came the primates. At about the same time, from a backward branch, came the ancestors of the apes; the human line kept moving forward, while the ape line stood still or went backward.
p61.020: One million years ago, two primitive human beings were suddenly born of the primates. They are the real ancestors of humankind. On that day Urantia was registered as an inhabited world. Our ancestors were born and grew up in the cold, hard conditions of the time when the third glacier was advancing. They spread into Europe in the warm periods between the glaciers.
p61.022: The glaciers dug out lakes, moved great boulders, and even changed the courses of rivers, leaving clear marks on the land. Five hundred thousand years ago, during the fifth glacier, the six colored races suddenly appeared from primitive humankind within a single generation, and at the same time the Planetary Prince (the heavenly leader sent to guide the planet) came to this world. Two hundred thousand years ago, as the last glacier was advancing, the Lucifer rebellion broke out, which had a great effect on the history of this world.
p61.023: The sixth and last glacier was the largest in North America. As this glacier drew back, the Great Lakes were formed. The harsh ice age wiped out many animals or changed them greatly, and in North America the horse and the saber-toothed tiger disappeared. Arctic plants and animals that fled up the mountains still remain today on high mountains such as the Alps.
p61.024: Thirty-five thousand years ago the ice age ended everywhere except the polar regions. This was at nearly the same time that Adam and Eve, the Material Son and Daughter, came to this world. So the story of the mammalian era, which spans fifty million years, leads up to our own day. The story of our ancestors, born in cold and hardship who still kept moving forward, shows that difficulties can make us stronger.
p62.002: About a million years ago the direct ancestors of humankind appeared from lemurlike mammals through three sudden changes, that is, mutations. These ancestors came mainly from the western, or American, life line, and the central life line that developed in Africa added its strength. This paper is the story of the birth of humankind, told in person by a Life Carrier who planted life on earth and watched over it.
p62.004: The early lemurs that became the ancestors of humankind were not directly related to today's gibbons or apes. Nor did they come from the modern lemurs; they branched off from a common ancestor that died out long ago.
p62.005: Millions of years ago the lemurs of North America crossed the Bering land bridge and slowly moved southwest along the coasts of Asia. At last they reached a pleasant land west of India. Later, as the coastline sank under the sea, this place became an isolated peninsula with no way in or out except to the north. From this almost paradise-like place came two great groups: one is the modern apes, and the other is humankind.
p62.007: A little more than a million years ago the dawn mammals suddenly appeared on this peninsula. They were small, quick animals about three feet tall, hairy, and chattering like monkeys, but they ate meat. For their bodies, their brains were larger than those of any animal of that time. They were very curious, they were glad when they accomplished something, they were affectionate toward their families, and they were faithful to their mates. They also had feelings close to shame and regret.
p62.008: Because they were small and quick to sense danger, their fear was strong, so they built their homes high in the trees to escape danger. The tendency to fear that humankind has began at this time. They liked to live in groups, but when disturbed they became very fierce, and as the superior groups survived, the species gradually improved. Then, only seventy generations later, the next great change took place.
p62.010: A superior pair of dawn mammals gave birth to twins, a boy and a girl, in their tree home. These twins were more than four feet tall, walked upright, and had thumbs much like human ones. They were bright from childhood and became the leaders of the group, and they began a primitive social organization and division of labor. Their children formed a new group called the mid-mammals. The mid-mammals were the first animals to store food and to build homes both in the trees and underground.
p62.011: The Urantia Book says that the ancestors of humankind barely escaped extinction many times. The greatest danger came when lightning struck the tree where a superior mid-mammal couple was sleeping. That couple survived and moved to a new home, and soon they gave birth to the most important twins. These twins were the first ancestors of the primates.
p62.012: At the same time another couple, inferior in body and mind, also had twins. These twins were interested only in eating, and they went south to warmer lands and became the ancestors of the modern apes. So man and the apes came from the same mid-mammal group, but not from the same parents. Man is descended from the most superior line, and the apes are descended from the most inferior pair.
p62.014: The primate twins walked upright from birth, grew to more than five feet tall, and had larger heads. They shared their meaning with each other by signs and sounds, but the rest of their family could not understand these. When they were about fourteen years old, they left the group, went west, and founded the new species of the primates.
p62.015: The primates had skeletons, hands, and feet very much like those of human beings, and they walked and ran as well as people do. But their fear was still great, so they slept in the trees at night, and they did not yet have a truly human mind. About twenty-one thousand years, or some nine hundred generations, after the dawn mammals appeared, two remarkable beings were suddenly born of the primates. They were the first true human beings.
p62.017: The first two human beings were born 993,419 years before the year 1934. They had fully human hands and feet, were fully grown at twelve, and could live about seventy-five years. New feelings appeared in them: admiration and pride, and, most wonderful of all, the feelings of worship such as awe, reverence, humility, and gratitude. They also had feelings such as sympathy, shame, love and hate, and jealousy.
p62.018: These twins were so full of curiosity and adventure that they nearly lost their lives many times. By about the age of ten they had made a language of signs and sounds with which they could share fifty ideas. Around the age of nine, on a clear day, the two held an important talk by a river and decided to live together and for each other. Heavenly beings watched this scene, but they did not control their minds. They only helped the twins go north to a safe place, following the decision the twins had made for themselves.
p62.019: Just before they left, their mother fearlessly gave her life to protect the twins from an attack by gibbons. After his children left, their father sank into deep grief, refused to eat, wandered through the forest, and died.
p62.021: The Life Carriers had been waiting for this day through long ages, ever since they first planted life in the sea. Animal mind had developed with the help of the seven adjutant mind-spirits (the seven spirit powers that help the minds of animals and people grow). First the spirit of intuition, which is instinct, worked, and then the spirits of understanding, courage, knowledge, and counsel worked one after another.
p62.022: But the two highest spirits had never yet worked. When the twins were about ten years old, the spirit of worship touched the mind of the girl for the first time, and soon after the mind of the boy. About a year later, when after careful thought the two made the purposeful decision to leave home and go north, the spirit of wisdom worked for the first time. From then on the two were recognized as beings with human minds.
p62.024: The day after the twins left, the universe communication circuit flashed for the first time, and on the third day the first message came from the universe headquarters. It said that mind of will dignity had appeared on Urantia and that the twins' choice to go north was “⟦Q 62:7.3⟧the first decision of mind—the human type of mind—on Urantia⟦/Q⟧”. This decision, it says, automatically opened the circuit.
p62.025: Next, the Life Carriers were instructed not to interfere from then on with the development of human beings. Since a will able to worship and to choose the path of ascension had appeared, their mission was over. Most of them left, and only a few remained, including the Life Carrier who tells this story. In this way Urantia was officially recognized as an inhabited planet. The fact that humankind began with one decision to choose the right path for itself reminds us how precious each of our choices is.
p63.002: When the first two human beings, the twins, were eleven years old, Urantia was registered as an inhabited planet. The message that came from the universe headquarters at this time announced that the parents of this new human race would be called Andon and Fonta, and said that it prayed they would soon receive the spirit of the Universal Father, the Thought Adjuster.
p63.003: Andon means “⟦Q 63:0.3⟧the first Fatherlike creature to exhibit human perfection hunger.⟦/Q⟧” and Fonta means, in the same way, “⟦Q 63:0.3⟧the first Sonlike creature to exhibit human perfection hunger.⟦/Q⟧” But the two did not know these names while they lived on earth. They called each other Sonta-an, meaning “⟦Q 63:0.3⟧loved by mother,⟦/Q⟧” and Sonta-en, meaning “⟦Q 63:0.3⟧loved by father.⟦/Q⟧” These were names full of care and respect for each other.
p63.005: Andon and Fonta were the most remarkable pair of human beings who ever lived on earth. These two, the parents of all humankind, were superior even to many of their descendants and were basically different from their ancestors. Their parents belonged to a fairly intelligent group that had been the first to learn to throw stones and fight with clubs.
p63.006: Andon made a weapon by tying a sharp flint to the end of a club with animal tendon, and with it he saved his own life and his sister's at least a dozen times. Their decision to leave the group shows a high level of mind. Their dim feeling that they were something more than animals came from the fact that they had personality, and it grew even stronger when the Thought Adjusters came to live in them.
p63.008: When they made up their minds to leave, the twins were afraid. They worried that they might disappoint their father and family, and that they might be attacked by the group, which was already jealous of them. Then one night, awakened by a fierce storm, the two held each other tight and decided to leave right away. They were terribly afraid of being on the ground at night, but they found the courage to set out at night, when there was less danger of being seen, and they safely reached the shelter they had prepared to the north.
p63.009: On the way, while chipping flint, Andon saw sparks fly. When autumn came and the nights grew cold, the two tried every day for two months to light a fire with flint, but they failed. At last, one evening, Fonta brought a dry bird's nest from a tree, and when the sparks fell on it, the nest burst into flame. It was the first time on earth that a creature had kindled a fire by itself. The two watched the fire all night long, dimly realizing that now they could overcome the cold and become forever independent of their animal relatives to the south.
p63.011: Almost two years after they left, their first child, Sontad, was born. Sontad was the first baby on earth to be wrapped in a warm covering at birth. The instinct to care lovingly for a helpless baby was a sign that an intelligent mind was growing. Andon and Fonta had nineteen children and lived to see fifty grandchildren and six great-grandchildren. The family lived together in a rock home dug out of soft limestone and joined by passageways.
p63.012: This family had a strong family spirit; they hunted together and tried not to scatter far apart. Andon and Fonta died at the age of forty-two, killed by falling rock in an earthquake. After that, Sontad led the family even with his injured foot, and he first piled up a heap of stones to bury the family members who had died. This family lived together for twenty generations and then began to scatter because of quarrels over food and other conflicts.
p63.014: The Andonites had dark eyes and dark skin with a reddish tinge, and in their looks they were most like today's Eskimos. They were the first creatures to keep out the cold with animal skins. They were good at imitating, but their play instinct was weak, and though they smiled, they did not laugh out loud. Humor was a gift left later by the descendants of Adam.
p63.015: The men fought bravely to protect their families, and the women cared for their children with love. In the way they would fight with one hand while protecting a wounded friend, the noble character of later humankind could be glimpsed ahead of time. Still, the heart that cares for others, that is, altruism, had not yet been born, and they did not think of making a better world for their grandchildren. Even so, they already had all the feelings needed for religion to arise.
p63.016: The Andonites developed a well-made language, and for a long time this language became the common language of humankind. But as their numbers grew, they set their minds only on hunting and revenge, and wars between the clans wiped out many of the best bloodlines. Because the Life Carriers know of such tendencies, they plan ahead to have humankind live divided into several races.
p63.018: At first the descendants of Andon did not go deep into Asia or into Africa but spread north and west. They built more than a thousand settlements along the great rivers throughout Europe, and on the banks of the Somme River in France they lived for tens of thousands of years. That is why many traces of them are found in this river valley. They lived in caves in riverside cliffs or hillsides, and they built round huts of stone and closed the entrances with stones at night.
p63.019: The Andonites were fearless hunters and ate mainly meat. Just as Andon had made a stone ax, his descendants made spear throwers and harpoons. In this way the mind that thinks up tools and the hand that uses them became one. They traveled far in search of good flint, just as people today search for gold or diamonds.
p63.021: For nearly ten thousand years the scattered Andonites fell further and further behind in culture and faith. Then a leader named Onagar appeared, brought peace among the tribes, and for the first time led them all to worship together the “⟦Q 63:6.1⟧Breath Giver to men and animals.⟦/Q⟧” Before that, Andon had almost come to worship fire, and people feared thunder and lightning or revered the great animals that served as their food. The ceremonies they held around the bodies of the animals they held in awe became the beginning of the later custom of offering sacrifices.
p63.022: The prayer Onagar taught begins, “⟦Q 63:6.6⟧O Breath of Life, give us this day our daily food⟦/Q⟧”. He stayed at a place called Oban, near today's Caspian Sea, and sent teachers far away to spread his teachings about one God and the “⟦Q 63:6.7⟧Great Beyond⟦/Q⟧”. They were the world's first missionaries, and they were also the first people to cook meat with fire.
p63.023: Onagar organized the tribes into a true society, and until the Planetary Prince came there was never again so noble a spiritual civilization. In this age many Thought Adjusters and guardian seraphim (angels who watch over people) came to Urantia. That is why this time is called the golden age of primitive man.
p63.024: 7. The Survival of Andon and Fonta
p63.025: Andon and Fonta, the parents of humankind, survived death, passed through the mansion worlds (the worlds of learning where people first wake up after death), and became citizens of Jerusem, and there they became one with their Thought Adjusters. Because they know the history of the human race they began, they grieved over the rebellion and failures this world went through, but they rejoiced greatly at the news that Michael had chosen to come to this world as a man.
p63.026: Now they serve on the first mansion world, welcoming the pilgrims of time, that is, people newly awakened after death. The story of these two, who overcame their fear and bravely chose a new path, is the most heroic chapter in the history of Urantia. And it reminds us that all of us are the descendants of that brave decision.
p64.002: This paper tells how the various races of humankind arose and spread, from the time of Andon and Fonta about a million years ago, through the age of the Planetary Prince (the heavenly leader sent to guide the planet), until the end of the ice age. The first half of human history is the age before the Planetary Prince came, and the second half begins with the coming of the Planetary Prince and the appearance of the six colored races. This later period overlaps almost exactly with what is usually called the Old Stone Age.
p64.004: Early humankind lived in a place closed in on every side. To the east was the high Tibetan plateau, to the south and west the wide sea, and to the north the advancing glaciers. Much of man's oldest religious feeling grew out of this sense of being hemmed in. Even so, the progressive Andonites did not go back to their animal relatives in the southern forests. The Urantia Book says that man has always fallen behind in the forest and has actually progressed in open country and in cold places, because cold and hunger trained him in hard work, invention, and wisdom.
p64.005: The descendants of Andon spread west as far as France and England and east as far as Java. But the groups that went east mixed a great deal with less advanced relatives, and as this happened, the settlements that worshiped God grew fewer, and the early civilization was in danger of disappearing.
p64.007: By about nine hundred thousand years ago, the culture and faith left by Andon and Onagar had almost disappeared, and even the skill of working flint had dropped to its lowest level. In Europe a people called the Heidelberg race had spread widely.
p64.008: Even in this dark time there were two groups that kept the traditions of Andon. One of them was the Foxhall peoples of England. They were the first people to live in England, and they kept up the skill of flintwork and a primitive faith. Their descendants later moved west and became the ancestors of today's Eskimos.
p64.010: The other was the Badonan tribes, who lived in the highlands of northwestern India. They were the only descendants of Andon who did not offer human sacrifices. They lived in stone houses and caves on a broad plateau with forests and streams. Watching their homeland slowly sink into the sea, they were terribly afraid of water, so they lived on high ground.
p64.011: About eight hundred fifty thousand years ago the Badonan tribes fought a long struggle with the animal-like groups around them, and as a result a race that appeared new came into being. These were the Neanderthal races.
p64.013: The Neanderthalers were excellent fighters and hunters; they spread from France to China and North Africa and held the world for almost half a million years. They ate reindeer, made clothing from skins, and made tools from horn and bone. They even fished by cutting holes in frozen rivers. When the glaciers advanced they withdrew to the south, and when the glaciers drew back they went north again.
p64.014: But during these long ages their culture made almost no progress, and spiritually it was a dark age. The Neanderthalers had no religion except superstition born of fear. They were terribly afraid of fog and darkness, and when the moonless nights came, they began to offer their finest people as sacrifices in hope that the moon would shine again. This terrible custom of human sacrifice went on for a very long time.
p64.016: Five hundred thousand years ago a war of more than a hundred years broke out among the Badonan tribes, and when it ended only about a hundred families were left. Then one couple among them suddenly began to have unusually intelligent children. This family was the Sangik family, the ancestors of the six colored races.
p64.017: The nineteen children of the Sangik family each took on a different skin color when exposed to sunlight: five were red, two orange, four yellow, two green, four blue, and two indigo. When they married within their own groups, their descendants also took after their parents' skin color. At about this time the Planetary Prince came to this world.
p64.018: 6. The Six Sangik Races of Urantia
p64.019: On an ordinary planet the colored races appear one at a time, in order, but on Urantia the six races came all at once from a single family. The red man was the first to create tribal civilization and government and invented the bow and arrow early, but he was weakened by a tendency to fight among his own people, was pushed back by the yellow man, and crossed over to North America. There a leader named Onamonalonton revived the worship of the “⟦Q 64:6.7⟧Great Spirit.⟦/Q⟧” The orange race loved to build anything and everything and piled up great heaps of stone, but in Africa it was destroyed by the green race.
p64.020: The yellow man was the first race to give up hunting, settle down, and farm. Because they built up brotherhood and learned to live in peace with one another, they survived in the greatest numbers, and Singlangton proclaimed the worship of the “⟦Q 64:6.15⟧One Truth.⟦/Q⟧” The green race scattered into many branches and grew weaker. The blue man was a great race who invented the spear and laid the foundations of many of the arts of modern civilization, and Orlandof revived the worship of the true God under the name of the “⟦Q 64:6.23⟧Supreme Chief.⟦/Q⟧” Today's white peoples are descendants of this blue man. The indigo race was the last to leave its homeland and settled in Africa, and in the days of Orvonon it went through a great spiritual awakening.
p64.021: The Urantia Book says clearly that the indigo peoples have “⟦Q 64:6.27⟧exactly the same standing before the celestial powers as any other earthly race⟦/Q⟧”. It also explains why there are many races. Variety stirs up healthy competition, and among different peoples it helps human generosity and the heart that cares for others to grow. Because of Caligastia's betrayal and the Lucifer rebellion, a dark age went on, but teachers who rose up here and there kept civilization from falling apart completely.
p64.023: As the Sangik descendants were growing in number, the glaciers spread widely, so for almost a hundred thousand years they lived close together near their homeland. After that the red man went northeast through Asia to North America, the yellow man went to eastern Asia, and the blue man went west to Europe. The orange, green, and indigo races crossed newly formed land bridges into Africa. The blue man who went to Europe mixed with the Neanderthalers and greatly improved them. The mixed groups who went with the red man to North America later built the civilizations of Mexico, Central America, and South America.
p64.024: When the last glacier advanced, the descendants of Andon crowded into southern England built boats and set out to sea. They were the first sea adventurers, and some of them reached Iceland and Greenland. Their descendants, the Eskimos, later crossed over to North America.
p64.025: The Life Carrier who wrote this paper regrets that much of the courage, firm perseverance, and splendid devotion of the early ancestors has been lost today. We who live in a comfortable civilization would do well to keep in our hearts the courage and perseverance our ancestors showed.
p65.002: This paper explains under whose care, and in what way, the evolution of life takes place. Life arises and grows through the teamwork of three groups: the physical controllers, who handle matter and energy; the Seven Master Spirits, who give life; and the Life Carriers, who plant life and tend it directly. In this way the bodies of living things are made ready to receive mind.
p65.003: The development of life has three stages. First the body becomes able to hold mind; next the adjutant mind-spirits (the seven spirit powers that help the minds of animals and people grow) nurture mind; and finally the Thought Adjuster comes and adds spirit to the human mind. Because these three groups work together, The Urantia Book says that evolution is always purposeful and “⟦Q 65:0.7⟧never accidental⟦/Q⟧”.
p65.005: The Life Carriers are special beings who can exist in three different forms. Ordinarily they work in a state about halfway between matter and spirit, but in this state they cannot make new life. So when they plant life, with the help of other heavenly beings they change their form to the material level and organize the life materials. Once life has begun, they go back to their usual state, and from then on they can no longer make new life but only care for the life that is growing.
p65.006: Then, when human beings with free will appear, the Life Carriers must either leave the planet or pledge not to meddle with evolution any more. Those who choose to stay change into a third, semispiritual state so that they can serve as advisers. The Life Carrier who wrote this paper has also stayed on Urantia in this state since the days of Andon and Fonta.
p65.008: The story of how man began with the seaweeds of the ocean and became master of the land is the story of a long struggle to survive. The most distant ancestor of humankind was the mud in the warm, shallow waters of the ancient seas. The in-between creatures that passed from plant to animal were like sponges, while bacteria and amoebas stayed just as they were in early times. Many disease-causing bacteria are backward life that lost their chlorophyll and became parasites.
p65.009: After that came animals such as jellyfish, starfish, insects, clams, and octopuses, and then fishes appeared. From fishes came frogs, from frogs came reptiles, and from reptiles came birds and mammals. The greatest leap was when reptiles became birds. Man evolved from mammals that came mainly from the western life line. It was not by chance but by plan that humankind appeared during the ice age, because the harsh cold was just right for raising up a hardy human race.
p65.011: The Life Carriers can make use of all the resources of nature and of chance opportunities to help life along, but they cannot mechanically interfere with evolution or manipulate it as they please. Just because the ancestral line of humankind was once held in a single frog and barely escaped extinction, we need not think only that humankind almost vanished. Even then the Life Carriers were caring for more than a thousand other lines at the same time. Even without Andon and Fonta, human beings would finally have appeared, though later.
p65.012: No new races arise from animals any more. Just as the Life Carriers cared for life until human beings appeared, now human beings must take up that work themselves. The Urantia Book says that man's evolutionary destiny “⟦Q 65:3.6⟧is in his own hands⟦/Q⟧”. It also encourages us that those with good ideas will one day, in the far future, have the chance to share those ideas in the work of tending the universe even better.
p65.014: Urantia was a life-experiment world, where life was designed a little differently. Here the Life Carriers perfected more than twenty-eight ways of improving life. Still, these were not experiments tried at random. For example, when the cells of our bodies are injured, the healthy cells nearby give off healing substances and make new cells to fill in the wound. The Life Carriers chose this way of healing after more than half a million experiments.
p65.015: Urantia had special features, too. The Andonites appeared before the six colored races, and the six races came from a single family at the same time. Human beings also came to have will much earlier than usual. On the other hand, in the course of these trials many in-between creatures that seemed useless also came into being.
p65.017: What the Life Carriers regret most is that their plans were badly shaken by Caligastia's betrayal and Adam's default. Also, a certain primitive plant went back to being a parasitic bacterium and brought many diseases to man. It was hoped that mixing with Adam's descendants would make people resistant to these diseases, but with Adam's default that hope also collapsed.
p65.018: Even so, The Urantia Book says that the universe is not run to please us, and that the wise ones who govern the universe know fully what they are doing. So it is right for us to be patient and co-operate. Just as Michael came to this world as a man, hardships bring rewards as well, and the heavenly supervisors firmly believe that humankind will triumph in the end.
p65.020: Because a scientist must kill life in order to analyze it, he can never reach the secret of living life. Within all life dwells an endless longing to become more perfect. Plants advanced by making chlorophyll and bearing seeds, and animals came to carry oxygen with the iron in their blood. Human teeth, too, are decreasing from thirty-six to thirty-two and now toward twenty-eight, which shows that evolution is still going on today.
p65.021: But physics and chemistry alone cannot fully explain human evolution. Physical laws do not learn, but mind can learn from experience. A creature with mind not only reacts to its environment but can also change it. The development of this mind depends on the help of the seven adjutant spirits.
p65.023: The seven adjutant spirits help the minds of intelligent beings lower than man. They have nothing to do with mechanical reactions; they begin to work from the moment the ability to learn by experience appears. Their help blends so smoothly with natural evolution that we feel the workings of mind simply as something natural. Because of its special life design, Urantia was a place where it was unusually hard for these spirits to make contact with mind.
p65.024: The adjutants help the growth of mind up to the sixth, the spirit of worship, and when the last, the spirit of wisdom, works, the ministry of higher spirit joins in. All these changes come about not suddenly but gradually and in harmony. The reactions of the body, the reactions of the mind, and the activities of the spirit are linked together, yet they are different realms.
p65.026: Why does evolution take so long? Because the Life Carriers cannot make life progress faster than the land and climate of the planet change. To us, whose lives are short, evolution seems long, but seen from timeless Paradise, it is not.
p65.027: Just as the growth of mind waits on the conditions of the body, the growth of spirit is affected by the growth of mind. But the growth of the soul does not depend on learning or culture. As long as there is a decision to do the will of the Father in heaven, the soul can grow. The Urantia Book says that if anyone sincerely desires to know God, to find him, and to become like him, no obstacle can defeat “⟦Q 65:8.5⟧the whole-souled choice of will⟦/Q⟧”. Our true growth depends, in the end, on what we choose.
p66.002: On an ordinary world, when the mind of primitive man develops the will to choose the path of eternal survival, the Planetary Prince (a Lanonandek Son sent to guide the planet) soon arrives. But on Urantia the Planetary Prince came only after almost half a million years had passed since human beings first had will.
p66.003: About five hundred thousand years ago, around the time the six colored races appeared, Prince Caligastia arrived. At that time almost five hundred million primitive human beings were living on earth, spread over Europe, Asia, and Africa. The Prince's headquarters was set up in the region of Mesopotamia, close to the very center of the world's population.
p66.005: Caligastia was a Lanonandek Son with much experience in governing the universe. Lucifer made him one of his assistants, and he did his work well. For a long time he had earnestly wanted to become a Planetary Prince, and after being turned down several times, he was at last sent to Urantia. But he always had a slightly restless temperament and a tendency to oppose the established order in small matters.
p66.006: The Melchizedek who wrote this paper was present on the day Caligastia departed. He thought that Urantia, receiving such a brilliant and experienced Prince, was one of the most fortunate planets. But at that time he did not notice that Caligastia “⟦Q 66:1.5⟧was insidiously falling in love with himself⟦/Q⟧”. This is how pride grows without being noticed.
p66.008: The Prince did not come alone. His associate, Daligastia, and many angels came with him. The most interesting of them were the corporeal staff known as the Caligastia one hundred. They were people who had lived and died on other planets and had risen as far as Jerusem, one hundred men and women chosen from among more than seven hundred eighty thousand who volunteered for this work.
p66.009: To work in this world they needed human bodies. So the Life Carriers called together one hundred men and women, the finest descendants of Andon and Fonta, transferred part of their life plasm, and made new bodies for the one hundred. The whole process took ten days. This event later became the root of many legends and was even mixed up with the story of Adam and Eve.
p66.011: The Prince's headquarters city was called Dalamatia, after Daligastia. It was a simple but beautiful city surrounded by a wall forty feet high. In the center of the city stood the temple of the unseen Father, and most of the buildings were one-story houses built of brick. Neighboring tribes took this city as their model and improved their own homes and villages.
p66.012: The greatest task of that age was to change hunters into herders of animals, and then into peace-loving farmers. The one hundred chose outstanding people from the surrounding tribes, taught them, and sent them back to their own tribes as teachers and leaders.
p66.013: 4. Early Days of the One Hundred
p66.014: The arrival of the one hundred made a great impression, and many myths grew out of the stories of this time. People could easily have taken them for gods, but the one hundred did not use supernatural methods. They had human bodies, but they were special beings. They lived on fruits and nuts rather than meat, and by eating the fruit of the tree of life sent from Edentia they could live for a long time without growing old.
p66.015: They were instructed not to have children. But in the thirty-third year after they came to Dalamatia, two of them, through a union of mind and soul, accidentally produced a new being invisible to human eyes. With the Prince's permission all of the one hundred did the same, and fifty thousand primary midwayers (invisible beings between humans and angels) came into being. They were a great help in the work of the headquarters.
p66.017: The one hundred worked in ten councils of ten each. The council of Ang taught the digging of wells, irrigation, and ways of storing food, so that people could prepare for famine. The council of Bon taught the taming of cattle and other animals and the use of the wheel. The council of Dan taught ways of protecting people from wild beasts, and the council of Nod taught the making of goods and trade between tribes.
p66.018: The council of Fad took charge of education and created the first alphabet, of twenty-five letters, and the library of Dalamatia held more than two million records. The council of Hap taught people to revere the Creator instead of fearing ghosts and gave them “⟦Q 66:5.14⟧the Father's prayer⟦/Q⟧”. That prayer asks, “⟦Q 66:5.15⟧Deliver us from the fear of all save you.⟦/Q⟧” The council of Lut taught healthy habits such as cooking food, washing the body, and taking in sunlight.
p66.019: The council of Mek taught the basics of the arts, such as pottery and sculpture, and of science. The council of Tut encouraged peaceful relations among the tribes and marriage only after the partners knew each other well. Finally, the supreme court led by Van served as the highest tribunal, overseeing the work of the other councils. Much of the knowledge learned at this time was lost after the rebellion and has been rediscovered only in modern times.
p66.021: At that time the world was tightly bound by old traditions. Tradition gives stability, but it can also block new ventures and creativity. The one hundred began to teach personal initiative, but that good rule was cut off far too soon.
p66.022: The one hundred did not try to change primitive humankind all at once, because they knew well that human beings progress slowly. The person who helped each tribe was always from that tribe, and they did not force the customs of other races on anyone. Instead they patiently raised up the good customs each people already had. The Urantia Book says their aim was “⟦Q 66:6.6⟧progression by evolution and not revolution by revelation⟦/Q⟧”. Teaching too much, too fast, only brings confusion.
p66.024: The one hundred formed couples of men and women and set up model homes. They had no children of their own, but they adopted and raised more than five hundred children from various tribes, many of them orphans. The system of a family settling in one place and living together began at this time. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 66:7.4⟧Savage man loves his child, but civilized man loves also his grandchild.⟦/Q⟧” In the schools, they learned both handwork and co-operation by learning through doing.
p66.025: Hap gave the seven commands called “⟦Q 66:7.8⟧The Father's Way⟦/Q⟧”. They include: do not fear any god but God, the Father of all; do not lie when on trial; do not kill; do not steal what belongs to your neighbor; and show respect to your parents and elders. It was also the teachers of Dalamatia who divided the week into seven days.
p66.026: The Urantia Book says clearly that farming is not a punishment for sin. Working the soil is not a curse but a great blessing, letting us enjoy the most human of activities. But in the confusion and darkness after the rebellion, nearly all the fine achievements of Dalamatia were lost.
p66.028: Caligastia had one outstanding weakness. He was too much of an individualist, he was uneasy under authority, and he was easily drawn to groups that complained. Lucifer and Caligastia were given loving advice many times about their critical attitude and their pride, but they mistook it for interference with their freedom. In the end this world, which had been progressing well for nearly three hundred thousand years, was thrown into great confusion by Caligastia's betrayal at the time of the Lucifer rebellion, and he was stripped of his authority.
p66.029: The Urantia Book makes an important point clear. Even though there was such a being as Caligastia, it is not true, as some teach, that a “⟦Q 66:8.6⟧devil⟦/Q⟧” can force a person's mind to do what that person does not want to do. “⟦Q 66:8.6⟧The free will of man is supreme in moral affairs⟦/Q⟧”, and even the Thought Adjuster does not force our choices. So what kind of person we will become depends, in the end, on our own choices. The story of Caligastia also reminds us how precious it is to accept advice humbly.
p67.002: To really understand the problems that people on Urantia, our Earth, face today, we need to know about a planetary rebellion that happened long, long ago. This huge event did not do much to stop the evolution of living bodies, but it greatly changed the direction of social progress and the path of people's spiritual growth.
p67.004: Caligastia was the Planetary Prince of Urantia, a universe leader put in charge of guiding one planet. About three hundred thousand years into his rule, Satan, Lucifer's assistant, came to inspect the planet. Satan was not a hideous monster but a shining being. He told Caligastia about the “⟦Q 67:1.2⟧Declaration of Liberty⟦/Q⟧” that Lucifer was preparing, and Caligastia promised to betray the planet once the rebellion began. No evil damages a personality more than betraying the people who trusted you. Because of this, Caligastia's personality became completely twisted.
p67.005: This section also explains different kinds of wrongdoing. Error is misunderstanding reality. Evil is knowing reality only in part and so failing to fit things together well. Sin is choosing on purpose to go against God's will, even when you know better. Iniquity is a state where that defiance goes on openly and the personality starts to fall apart. If sin is repeated, it becomes a habit, and it can easily slide into iniquity. Every sin can be forgiven, but someone hardened in iniquity finds it very hard to truly repent.
p67.007: One midwinter, Caligastia held a long conference with his associate Daligastia. Soon Daligastia called the leaders of the planet together and demanded that they hand over all their authority, because Caligastia was going to proclaim himself absolute sovereign of Urantia. Van, the chairman of the supreme council of coordination, bravely spoke up against this. He declared that it was rebellion and appealed to Lucifer, the system sovereign. But Lucifer took Caligastia's side instead. Van spoke for seven hours, accusing them of ignoring the sovereignty of the universe of Nebadon, and he asked the Most Highs of Edentia for help.
p67.008: Right then the circuits connecting the planet with the universe were cut, and Urantia was completely isolated. Daligastia proclaimed Caligastia “⟦Q 67:2.4⟧God of Urantia⟦/Q⟧”. Now the angels and other celestial beings all had to choose between Lucifer's way and the Father's will. This struggle went on for more than seven years, and the authorities of Edentia did not step in until everyone had made their own decision.
p67.010: When the rebellion became known, the whole system of Satania was quarantined from the other systems. There was “⟦Q 67:3.1⟧war in heaven⟦/Q⟧”, and it spread to many planets. On Urantia, only forty members of the Prince's staff of one hundred, including Van, refused to join the rebellion. Almost half of the seraphim, and more than forty thousand of the midway creatures, the beings who stand between humans and angels, sided with Caligastia. The loyal ones gathered in a small village east of Dalamatia and guarded the tree of life.
p67.011: These seven years were a time for searching hearts and training souls. The person who shone brightest during this time was Amadon. He was an ordinary human who helped Van. Caligastia had a brilliant mind and great universe experience, yet he lost his way. Amadon, on the other hand, had little learning and little experience, but he was not swayed by Daligastia's clever words and stayed loyal to the end. Only after everyone had decided did the Most Highs of Edentia and the Melchizedeks come and take charge of Urantia.
p67.012: 4. The Caligastia One Hundred after Rebellion
p67.013: In the end, it turned out that groups such as Van's court, the college of revealed religion, and the council on art and science had stayed loyal, while groups such as Nod's commission on industry and trade had joined the rebellion. The loyal forty were later taken to Jerusem and started again on the path to Paradise. The rebel sixty made Nod their leader, but they lost the power that had kept them alive, and in the end they became beings who would die. They moved away to the north and east, and their descendants came to be called the Nodites.
p67.014: When these superhuman beings married humans, legends arose about gods coming down and marrying people. Much of the idol worship of later times also began from wanting to remember them. The Urantia Book says it believes that many of the beings who were fooled by the rebellion have already sincerely repented, and that someday, in some way, they will return to universe service.
p67.016: For about fifty years after the rebellion, Dalamatia was in great confusion. Instead of slow progress, Caligastia tried to change the world all at once, and for primitive tribes who were not ready, liberty quickly turned into license. As a result, society fell back to its old level, and progress had to start over from the beginning. One hundred and sixty-two years after the rebellion, a great tidal wave swept in, and Dalamatia sank under the sea. By then the people left there had already turned the temple of the Father into a place for worshiping false gods.
p67.018: Van and his followers withdrew to the highlands west of India and made plans to rebuild the world. After the loyal staff left, Amadon and the loyal humans with him, the Amadonites, carried on the work. They grew in number and became the “⟦Q 67:6.3⟧biologic leaven⟦/Q⟧” that supplied the world with leaders through the long dark ages after the rebellion.
p67.019: After that, Urantia was governed for a long time by a council of planetary receivers made up of twelve Melchizedeks, and Van worked faithfully alongside them. Within less than a thousand years after the rebellion, he had set up more than three hundred and fifty advanced groups all around the world. With the help of the tree of life, Van and Amadon lived for more than one hundred and fifty thousand years, and after Adam and Eve arrived they were taken to Jerusem. Edentia's ruling on Van's appeal, though, never got through because the communication lines had been cut; it was found only recently inside an energy transmitter.
p67.021: When someone deliberately keeps rejecting the light, the results for that person's soul are a matter only between that person and God. But the outward effects of sin reach all the beings around them. In fact, for fifty thousand years after the rebellion, humankind made almost no progress. The universe is all connected, so everyone shares, to some degree, in the troubles of one.
p67.022: But here is something important. No one's sin can take away another person's right to live forever. Eternal survival depends only on the decisions of your own mind and the choices of your soul. Because of the rebellion and Adam's default, humanity's intellectual and social progress was badly delayed, but no one can stop the spiritual growth of a person who wants to know God and do his will. As The Urantia Book puts it, sin is “⟦Q 67:7.7⟧wholly personal⟦/Q⟧” in its spiritual consequences.
p67.023: 8. The Human Hero of the Rebellion
p67.024: Many brave beings stood against the Lucifer rebellion, but the universe records name Amadon as the most outstanding figure in the whole system of Satania. For seven years, the question the celestial beings of the universe asked every day was this: “⟦Q 67:8.3⟧What of Amadon of Urantia, does he still stand unmoved?⟦/Q⟧” The Urantia Book says that the steadfast loyalty of Amadon and his 143 companions did more good in the universe than all the evil and sorrow the rebellion caused.
p67.025: God calls the future workers of Paradise from among ordinary humans just like Amadon. Amadon became a hero not because he was clever or experienced, but because his heart held on to what was right to the very end. We too, when we refuse to be easily swayed by the words around us and stay true to the right path, can become a great light, even if we are small.
p68.002: Starting with this paper, a long story unfolds: how humankind began at a time when people were not very different from animals and little by little built civilization. The first thing to remember is that civilization is not something you inherit automatically at birth. Precious things like science, philosophy, and religion are not passed down through our genes, so every child has to learn them fresh, and every generation has to be educated all over again. The teachers of Dalamatia were the first to teach people how to live by working together.
p68.004: Primitive people did not naturally overflow with brotherly love for one another. Instead, they learned through bitter experience that “⟦Q 68:1.1⟧in union there is strength⟦/Q⟧”. A person who wandered alone was easily attacked, but someone who belonged to a tribe was safe, because the tribe would take revenge on anyone who harmed him. That is why The Urantia Book calls civilization humanity's insurance against violent death, and says the premium is keeping the rules of society.
p68.005: People found out that if a hundred of them joined their strength with one mind, they could move even a huge stone. Society did not come about just because many people gathered in one place, but because they cooperated wisely with each other. Cooperation is not an inborn trait. People learned it, at first out of fear, and later because it was the most profitable way to live. The groups that joined together early survived better, and thanks to this, civilization kept moving forward in spite of many mistakes.
p68.007: Society progressed faster the more it succeeded in reducing the dangers and pains of life. The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 68:2.2⟧Self-maintenance originates society, while excessive self-gratification destroys civilization.⟦/Q⟧” The great forces that first brought people together were hunger and love, and the forces that kept them bound together were vanity and fear, especially fear of ghosts. For a very long time, human history was a struggle to get enough to eat, and The Urantia Book warns that today's society struggles instead because of too much luxury and greed.
p68.008: The home was another important starting point. Because helpless babies needed care, men and women divided up their work, and wherever the woman was became the home. Yet in primitive times women had to gather food, carry loads, and put up with harsh treatment. Even so, the home was humanity's first successful peace group, and nearly all the lasting values of civilization came from the home. The desire to show off, which is vanity, gathered people in front of a stage and became the root of art, ceremonies, and athletic games, but too much of it can bring civilization down.
p68.010: For primitive people, dreams about ghosts were a terrifying experience. Animals do not imagine a life after death, but humans were afraid of the spirits of the dead. This fear bound people together even more tightly and made society more orderly. This baseless fear later prepared people to discover “⟦Q 68:3.3⟧the fear of the Lord which is the beginning of wisdom⟦/Q⟧”. The empty fears of evolution are meant to be replaced by the awe for God that comes through revelation.
p68.011: But hunger, love, vanity, and fear alone cannot overcome the suspicion and quarrels between people. In fact, these same forces sometimes drive people into war. Humanity's peaceful spirit is not something we are born with. It comes from the teachings of revealed religion, from experience built up over time, and above all from the teachings of Jesus, the Prince of Peace.
p68.013: All the social institutions we have today grew out of the customs of our distant ancestors. Just as a person has habits, a group has customs, and as these piled up they became the mores, the rules of living that a society keeps. Primitive people believed that dead ancestors punished anyone who broke the rules, so they followed their customs even more strictly. From morning to night, a primitive person had to do everything exactly according to custom; he was a slave to custom.
p68.014: That does not mean customs are only bad. Customs are like the thread that holds civilization together, so a hasty revolution that tries to overturn everything at once is almost fatal to civilization. Changing little by little toward better customs is the way a society survives. Of course, not every change was for the better, and human history has seen many steps backward too.
p68.016: The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 68:5.1⟧Land is the stage of society; men are the actors.⟦/Q⟧” The skill people use to work the land, together with their standard of living, determines their culture. Civilization moved forward in four stages. First was the collection stage, when people gathered whatever food they could find. Second was the hunting stage, when people made weapons by tying stones to the ends of sticks and hunted animals. Third was the pastoral stage, when people tamed animals and lived by their herds. Fourth was the agricultural stage, when people grew plants for food.
p68.017: In the pastoral age, once men could get food from their herds, they became independent of women, and women's position dropped sharply. Agriculture produced the highest material civilization and made it possible to feed far more people from the same land. Adam and Eve, too, were people who tended a garden. Hunters and herders loved to fight, but growing plants builds patience and peace. The Urantia Book says that even an industrial age must stand on a foundation of sound agriculture.
p68.019: Humans are children of nature, made from the soil, and humanity's basic struggle has always been for land. Through skill, people increased what the land produced and gained the free time to develop culture. When land was plentiful, each person was valued, but when land ran short and people became many, life was treated as cheap and the bad side of human nature came out. Cities greatly magnify the powers of the people who live in them, whether for good or for evil.
p68.020: The Urantia Book explains that primitive tribes had a terrible custom of abandoning or killing weak babies to keep their numbers down. But once a mother had nursed a child, the child was almost never killed, because a mother's love was that strong. The Urantia Book says that in the future the population problem will test the wisdom of world leaders, and it calls the healthy, stable ordinary person the “⟦Q 68:6.11⟧backbone of civilization⟦/Q⟧”. Civilization was built step by step by ordinary people working together and learning. What we learn and do together today is also part of that long story.
p69.002: Humans differ from animals in that they can enjoy humor, art, and religion. They also differ in that they make tools, share their thoughts with each other, and set up institutions. An institution is a set way of doing things, or an organization, that a society keeps going for a long time. Whenever people live together for long, institutions always appear, and if you look at their roots, they all began as old customs that piled up and became traditions.
p69.004: Every institution does work that society needs, but when it grows too big, it can easily hide each person's individuality and initiative. That is why The Urantia Book says people should not be dragged around by their institutions but should be in control of them. Human institutions fall into three groups. The first are the institutions of self-maintenance, which come from hunger and the instinct to stay alive, such as industry, property, and government. The second are the institutions of self-perpetuation, which come from love and the mother instinct, such as marriage and the home, schools, education, ethics, and religion. The third are the practices of self-gratification, which come from the wish to show off and have fun, such as dress and decoration, dancing, entertainment, and games. These three are woven together to make one society.
p69.006: Primitive industry grew slowly, like an insurance against famine. People began by learning from animals that store up food in good seasons. The Urantia Book says that poverty is the natural condition of humans, and that wealth comes from labor, knowledge, and organization. Primitive people disliked hard work and were never in a hurry. The idea of finishing a job within a set time is a very recent one.
p69.007: Planned, purposeful work is what sets humans apart from animals. The Urantia Book says that the need to work is the greatest blessing for humans. All the members of the Prince's staff worked, and Adam tended the Garden. Primitive people were like gamblers who wanted to get something without effort, and they often gave the credit for success to their charms. But little by little, magic gave way to foresight, self-control, and hard work.
p69.009: The work of primitive society was divided up step by step. First it was divided by sex: women took on the everyday tasks, and men took on hunting and fighting. Next, old people and those with disabled bodies made tools and weapons. The medicine man was the first specialist excused from physical labor, and the smiths who worked metal also became a special group. Masters and slaves came from the winners and losers of war, and work was also divided according to each person's different talents.
p69.010: After that came specialists such as flint workers, stonemasons, potters, and salt sellers. The first people to trade were women, and later a merchant class arose that took profits. The exchange of goods through barter grew into commerce.
p69.012: At first, taking things from others by force was common, but little by little, trading goods took its place. In the earliest trading, armed traders silently left their goods on either side of a wall wide enough to keep them from reaching each other, and so made their exchanges. Later, marketplaces appeared where people met without weapons, and these markets also became places of refuge where no one could be attacked.
p69.013: The first unit of weight was a grain of wheat, and fish, goats, and later cattle served as money. Even our writing today began with trade records, and the first written work of humans was an advertisement for salt. Through traders, new ideas and better methods spread around the world. In this way commerce became a great carrier of civilization that linked different cultures together.
p69.015: Capital is the fruit of labor that is saved up for the future by giving up some pleasure now. Storing up food taught people self-control. People gathered property for many reasons: to prepare for famine, to take care of their families, to show off, to gain high position and power, and out of worry about what would happen after death. In olden times, people sometimes lent money at one hundred percent interest a year and made others into slaves of debt.
p69.016: The Urantia Book says that while people's methods change, their nature hardly changes at all. Capital made society more complicated, but it is the foundation of today's industrial society, and thanks to capital and invention, the present generation enjoys more freedom than any before it. Of course, this does not mean it is right for selfish people to misuse capital.
p69.018: Learning how to make fire separated humans from animals once and for all. Since all animals feared fire, people were safe even at night, and they gathered around the fire to talk. Fire could be shared with a neighbor without losing any of your own, so it was the first way people could help others without any loss to themselves. The early home was not a building but a family gathered around the fire.
p69.019: Andon, who discovered fire, did not worship it, but many of his descendants thought fire was sacred and considered putting it out a sin. Once people cooked with fire, less energy was needed to digest food, and more energy was left over for culture. Fire later opened the way to metalworking, steam, and electricity.
p69.021: At first, all animals were enemies of humans. People ate animals, and then little by little learned to tame them and put them to work. The first animal to be tamed was the dog. It started with a dog that followed a hunter home, and thanks to watchdogs, whole families could sleep peacefully at night. But after people began keeping animals, many tribes treated women as roughly as beasts of burden. The Urantia Book says that the history of the mistreatment of women is one of the darkest chapters in human history.
p69.022: 8. Slavery as a Factor in Civilization
p69.023: Primitive people did not hesitate to make others into slaves, and women were the first slaves. In very ancient times, prisoners of war were killed or even eaten, so The Urantia Book explains that making captives into slaves was a step forward from that. It also says that rules and government arose in order to manage slavery. But The Urantia Book states clearly that slavery was oppressive and was the gravest evil, one that ate away at society from the inside.
p69.024: Today, with the invention of machines, slavery has almost disappeared. But many people, because of greed, make themselves slaves of debt. The Urantia Book says that the ideal of society is freedom for everyone, but that those who can work should do at least their own share of the work. Humans climbed upward by borrowing the power of fire, animals, and slaves, and now they are searching nature for the secrets of new energy.
p69.026: Primitive society was a community where everything was shared. This protected people from extreme poverty, but it encouraged laziness and crushed hard work and ambition. So it gradually broke down before strong human desires, such as the wish to pass things on to your family, the longing for freedom and leisure, and the wish for security. The Urantia Book says that it was the teachers of revealed religion who first announced that the poor could be saved just as well as the rich.
p69.027: Private property began with things a person had handled, charms, sleeping places, and wells and water holes, and when people took up farming, land too became a person's own. The Urantia Book says that property rights are not absolute, but that today's law, order, and freedom have grown up around private property. It also advises that when we change society, we should make sure we are changing it for the better. As it says, “⟦Q 69:9.18⟧Go forward, not backward!⟦/Q⟧” We too can treasure what our ancestors worked so hard to achieve, and step by step build a better world.
p70.002: Once people had more or less solved the problem of making a living, the next need was to manage the relationships between people. As industry developed, law and order became necessary, and once individuals owned property, government became necessary. In an evolving world, conflict is natural, and peace is kept only when there are social rules. Government was not designed by anyone; it grew slowly through trial and error.
p70.004: The Urantia Book says that war is the natural state of evolving humans, and that peace is the yardstick that measures how far civilization has advanced. War is an animal reaction to misunderstanding and irritation. The Andonites learned the golden rule early and settled their quarrels peacefully. Sometimes the two sides struck a tree with sticks, and whoever's stick broke first lost. Other times they held a public contest of insulting each other, and the spectators' applause decided the winner.
p70.005: The causes of early wars were hunger, stealing women, the vanity of showing off a tribe's power, the desire to capture slaves, revenge, sport, and religion. Ancient tribes fought cruel wars in the name of their gods, but The Urantia Book states clearly that God did not encourage such cruelties. As time went on, rules grew up for sparing prisoners, protecting women and those who did not fight, and declaring war ahead of time. A hostile spirit changes into a friendly one only very slowly.
p70.007: The Urantia Book explains that in the past, war also built up discipline, cooperation, and courage, and spread new ideas quickly. But war is like a very costly and dangerous medicine that sometimes kills the patient and wrecks society. Today war only destroys culture and gives no gain at all to make up for its terrible losses. Just as doctors of long ago gave up bloodletting and found better treatments, nations too must find better solutions than war.
p70.008: The Urantia Book warns that even an industrial age has its dangers, such as a mind that chases only material things, the worship of money and power, luxury, and laziness. It also says, “⟦Q 70:2.19⟧Do not make the mistake of glorifying war⟦/Q⟧”. War will disappear only when peaceful ways are worked out to take over the jobs war has done. From now on, when society looks for leaders, it must look for them not in war but in industry, science, and social achievement.
p70.010: In the most primitive herds, the herd was everything, but little by little families appeared, and above them clans and tribes. Relatives gathered into clans, and clans gathered into tribes living in one region. What tied these groups together in peace was trade. The Urantia Book says that world peace will be reached better through international trade than through sentimental peace plans.
p70.011: In olden times, strangers were always viewed with suspicion. So a ceremony of drinking each other's blood was used to take an outsider into the clan, and this later changed into sharing a drink of wine. When a guest left, a dish was broken in half and one piece was given to him, and guests paid for their lodging by telling stories of their travels. The first peace treaties were the “⟦Q 70:3.10⟧blood bonds⟦/Q⟧”, in which people shared each other's blood.
p70.013: The first peace group was the family, then came the clan, the tribe, and the nation, which became the state of today. It is very hopeful that the circle of peace has grown beyond blood relatives to include a whole nation. A clan was a group of people who had the same ancestors, the same language, and the same enemies. Clans were useful for governing their own local area, but they slowed down the rise of large, strong nations.
p70.015: The first true organ of government was the council of the elders. Old people with much wisdom and experience gathered to interpret the customs, make new rules, and carry them out. You could say that the three jobs of government today, judicial, legislative, and executive, were already present there. Some tribes even had women's councils or women rulers.
p70.016: But a war could not be fought by meetings alone. An army led firmly by one person fought better, so The Urantia Book says, “⟦Q 70:5.5⟧War has always been a kingmaker.⟦/Q⟧” A chief who at first commanded only in wartime gradually came to hold power in peacetime too. In some places there was a separate peace chief who acted as judge and teacher, and in other places medicine men ruled.
p70.018: Effective government of a nation began when chiefs with full authority appeared. Kingship grew out of a father's authority, and to avoid the confusion that came each time a king died, the throne came to be passed down. People thought of kings as sacred and feared them. Someone was needed to stand in for a king so sacred that he seldom appeared in public, and this was the origin of the prime minister. Starting with the officer in charge of food, many ministers came into being. Even the most cruel tyrants were held in check by medicine men, nobles, and the rebellions of the common people.
p70.020: After the clans bound together by blood, groups called secret societies arose. At first they were religious groups, but later they also helped to govern society. Boys at puberty left their parents and received years of strict training in these groups, where they were taught to control themselves and not to covet other men's wives. In later times, groups for girls also appeared, preparing them to be wives and mothers.
p70.021: Clubs without secrets actually became the first schools. Secret societies also acted as night police or spies, and they made bad kings uneasy. The first political parties grew out of these groups, and they were also used to collect taxes. Later they became the forerunners of the first charities and of the church, and some grew into international brotherhoods that reached beyond the tribe.
p70.023: Because people differ in their abilities and situations, classes appear in society. The Urantia Book says that the only worlds without classes are the most primitive ones and the most advanced ones. Classes arose for many reasons, such as birth, ability, war, wealth, where people lived, occupation, religion, race, and age.
p70.024: The Urantia Book explains that classes people can move between are needed in a progressing society, but when classes harden into castes that cannot change, personal growth and cooperation are blocked. It also says that the walls between classes will be torn down over a long time through things like education and the religious understanding that all people are brothers. Religion is a strong lever for lifting civilization, but it works with full power only when it has a fulcrum of sound minds.
p70.026: Nature gives people no rights; it gives only life and a world to live in. The greatest gift society gives people is security. Society tries to guarantee things such as food supply, national defense, internal peace, the family, property, the education of youth, fair conditions of work, and freedom of religion. The Urantia Book explains that human rights are not something we are simply born with, but are “⟦Q 70:9.13⟧the rules of the game⟦/Q⟧” that society agrees on together, and that they change over time.
p70.027: The Urantia Book says that the ideal of equality is a product of civilization, not of nature. Society cannot give everyone the same things, but it can promise to deal fairly with each person's rights. It is society's duty to give every person a fair and peaceful chance to make a living, to build a family, and to enjoy a certain amount of happiness.
p70.029: In nature there are only results that follow from causes; there is no justice as people mean it. When someone died, primitive people asked “⟦Q 70:10.3⟧not what killed him, but who?⟦/Q⟧” and they did not forgive even accidents. Medicine men and priests decided guilt by cruel tests with poison or fire. The Urantia Book states clearly that no divine being ever taught such unfair methods.
p70.030: Ancient society took revenge for granted, as in “⟦Q 70:10.9⟧an eye for an eye⟦/Q⟧”, but the teachers of revealed religion taught that vengeance belongs to the Lord. Little by little, fines and compensation took the place of revenge. True justice begins when vengeance is taken out of the hands of individuals and families and handed over to society and the state. People also learned that punishment that is sure and swift prevents crime better than punishment that is harsh.
p70.032: Drawing a sharp line between customs and laws is as hard as pointing to the exact moment at dawn when night turns into day. When customs build up over a long time, they become clear laws. Law begins as prohibitions that say 'do not,' and as civilization advances, it becomes law that gives direction and says 'do.' Judges of long ago had no written laws, so they simply said, “⟦Q 70:11.6⟧It is the custom.⟦/Q⟧”
p70.033: The first courts were fistfights with set rules, and the judge was more like a referee. Only later did people argue with words instead of fists. The Urantia Book says that you can tell a great deal about the level of a civilization by how fair its courts are and how honest its judges are.
p70.035: In the development of government, the biggest struggle has been over gathering power in one place. Universe administrators know from experience that representative government, in which the people choose representatives to govern, with the executive, legislative, and judicial branches in balance, is best suited to evolving worlds. The Urantia Book says that people should make their own constitution and should choose the most capable and moral persons as their leaders and judges.
p70.036: To protect liberty, dangers such as the unfair monopoly of power, demagogues and dictators, the tyranny of minorities, the failure of fairness, the union of church and state, and the loss of personal liberty must be prevented. The Urantia Book says that there is an ideal form of government, but it is not given by revelation; people must discover it slowly by working together. A good society does not come by itself, so we too can prepare ourselves to become wise and fair citizens.
